observations.seen: Day and dusk frames have flat, even key light with weak directional contrast. The night frame tints everything blue and leaves the rocks nearly black, but there is no rim separation on the targets.
Day frames show almost no cast shadows from props, crates, or the windmill. The night frame has hard, dark shadows inside the craters but little contact shadowing under the structures.
Materials look matte throughout. The barrel hoops and stone show no environment reflection, and the sky color does not carry into surface response.

The floating island diorama has photoscanned rocks, a water ring and grass tufts. The flat bright-green ground with cone trees and darker crater discs reads as placeholder next to the high-detail rocks.
There is a faint horizon haze in the day and dusk frames, and the night frame has a star field. There is no volumetric light, particles, or depth fog to tie the layers together.
Photogrammetry rock textures clash with the untextured flat-shaded grass and the low-poly cones. Wood crates and the barrel are decent, but the stone arch is cartoon-toon in style.
Assets come from mixed sources: realistic rocks, stylized windmill and arch, a lumpy orange blob on top of the arch, and low-poly cone foliage. There is no unified asset language.
The slingshot and the targets sit as small elements at the far left and right edges. A large empty green foreground takes up the lower half, and the rocks dominate the frame.
The camera is a fixed low-angle three-quarter perspective, not the elevated top-down framing. The foreground ground wastes screen space, and the subjects are tiny and pushed to the edges.
There is mild soft bloom on the horizon and a cool tint at night. Otherwise no grading, vignette, or AO depth is visible; the image looks mostly raw.
Clean, readable HUD: a parchment score card, a level title banner, egg ammo slots with a selection highlight, and a control hint bar.
